summary: AE + SE from Redwood and ZenHealth technical + security leads scoped POC acceptance criteria focused on quality evaluation. Agreed to a two-track plan: run hosted baseline benchmarks (latency/cost/throughput) and a quality eval using golden prompts/regression tests for hallucination/format checks. Success defined by quality thresholds (>= 0.85 weighted quality score), acceptable latency (p95 < 450ms for short prompts), and no PHI leakage in outputs. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Rachel Kim (CTO, ZenHealth), Carlos Rivera (Head of ML), Aisha Khan (Product), Samir Patel (Security), Jenna Ortiz (Data Eng)

Summary: Quick POC scoping for a quality-focused evaluation plan. Discussed success criteria, dataset and workload sizing, benchmark design (latency, throughput, cost), and detailed quality checks (golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks). Agreed owners and near-term next steps.

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey team, thanks for joining, we have about 50 minutes. Quick intros please.
[00:10] Rachel (CTO): Rachel here, hi. We're trying to evaluate Redwood for clinical summarization and triage workflows, main constraints are HIPAA, latency, and hallucination sensitivity.
[00:25] Carlos (ML): Yeah our core ask is: can we get reliably accurate summaries from discharge notes and structured outputs for downstream systems. We'll run a POC to validate quality and cost.
[00:38] Maya: Great. Liam from our SE team will drive the eval design, we'll also propose Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs. Any immediate hard constraints?
[00:47] Samir (Security): HIPAA is non-negotiable. We need KMS integration, private networking (VPC peering), audit logs. Also retention policy needs to be configurable.
[00:58] Liam (SE): Noted. On the quality plan: typically we do a golden prompt + regression harness. We'll start with 10-50 golden examples that represent critical cases — edge cases, short notes, long discharge summaries, and structured coding outputs.
[01:15] Aisha (Product): Can you explain golden prompts vs regression tests?
[01:20] Liam: Sure — golden prompts are specific input-output pairs we expect the model to match or be very close to; regression tests are a larger set of examples we run each model/version against to look for quality delta across releases. Golden set = high-signal, low-variance; regression set = broader coverage and metrics.
[01:36] Carlos: What metrics do you typically use? Exact match? ROUGE? Clinically-focused metrics?
[01:42] Liam: For summarization we suggest a combination: semantic similarity (BERTScore/embedding cosine), ROUGE-L for structure, plus task-specific heuristics like presence/absence of PHI, hallucination flags, and a downstream extractor test — does the structured extractor find the expected fields? We recommend a weighted score.
[02:00] Maya: Example weighting we've used: 60% quality (semantic + extractor accuracy), 25% hallucination/PHI safety (penalty-heavy), 15% format/structure compliance. We set a passing threshold, e.g., weighted score >= 0.85.
[02:15] Rachel: So hallucination gets a big penalty. How do you detect hallucinations at scale?
[02:20] Liam: Combination of heuristics and human spot checks. Heuristics: citation mismatch (for referenced IDs), contradictions to input (detect via QA model), and entity hallucination checks (compare entity mentions against input or external canonical lists). We'll include noise prompts to surface instability.
[02:36] Carlos: For acceptance, we need also quantifiable latency and throughput — operational constraints.
[02:40] Maya: Right. For the POC we'll run two benchmark passes: hosted baseline (to get a quick feel for latency and cost) and then optionally a Dedicated run that mimics committed capacity. Benchmarks will include: p50/p95/p99 latency for typical short prompts (50–150 tokens) and long prompts (2k tokens), tokens/sec for batching scenarios, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:05] Jenna (Data Eng): What about workload sizing? We currently expect ~5M tokens/day for the triage pipeline and spikes up to 10M on peak days.
[03:14] Liam: That's helpful. For 5M tok/day we recommend a dedicated baseline of N GPUs (we'll size more precisely after seeing token distribution), but for quick POC hosted is fine. We'll simulate traffic with similar request-size distributions and batching to measure latency.
[03:30] Maya: On QC tests: format checks are essential for you since outputs feed downstream systems. We'll add strict schema checking for fields like diagnosis codes, dates, medication lists. Fail any output that doesn't conform.
[03:44] Aisha: How will you capture false positives where the model returns plausible but wrong codes?
[03:48] Liam: We'll run extractor models to pull codes and then validate against input or controlled vocabularies; mismatches increment hallucination counters. Also include human review for a sample to calibrate thresholds.
[04:05] Samir: Security note: we need to make sure no PHI is retained in logs during hosted runs. Can you provide details on retention and KMS?
[04:12] Maya: Yes — we'll send our security whitepaper. Hosted runs can be configured with strict retention and encryption at rest; for maximum control Dedicated or Private deployment with VPC and customer KMS is available. We'll include SOC2 and encryption docs.
[04:27] Rachel: Timeline — we're targeting a decision within 6 weeks. We want a small pilot in that window with measurable pass/fail criteria.
[04:33] Maya: That aligns. Proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) — share SOW & POC plan; Week 1 — ZenHealth shares sample data and golden examples; Week 2 — Redwood runs hosted baseline benchmarks and seeds eval harness; Week 3 — run regression tests and human review; Week 4 — joint review and decision. We can compress if sample data is ready.
[04:55] Carlos: For the scoring approach can you be concrete? We need reproducible numbers in the SLO.
[05:00] Liam: Concrete example: Build per-example sub-scores: semantics (0-1 via embedding cosine, thresholded), extractor accuracy (0-1 exact or F1), format compliance (binary 0/1 or percent of fields correct), hallucination penalty (-0.5 to -1 severity per incident). Then aggregate: WeightedScore = 0.6*mean(semantics+extractor)/2 + 0.25*(1 - hallucination_rate) + 0.15*format_compliance. Pass if WeightedScore >= 0.85 and hallucination_rate < 2%. We'll provide the scoring script in python for reproducibility.
[05:36] Aisha: How many regression examples should we include?
[05:40] Liam: For initial run 2k-5k examples is good: large enough to statistically surface regressions but small enough to run frequently. Golden set maybe 30-100 critical cases.
[05:52] Jenna: Can Redwood host the eval harness or do we need to run locally?
[05:56] Maya: We can host the harness in a secured sandbox, or provide a reproducible repo you run. For HIPAA-sensitive data customers often prefer to run the eval internally. Option: we run a de-id subset for hosted baseline, then you run final regression internally on-prem.
[06:15] Samir: If you run hosted, how do we ensure de-id is adequate?
[06:18] Liam: We'll share de-id tooling and guidelines; also include sampling and human verification step. Reinforce that logs can be disabled and retention set to zero.
[06:30] Carlos: What about model deltas — you mentioned regression tests catch version drifts. If we upgrade model mid-POC, how do we handle comparisons?
[06:36] Liam: We'll pin model versions for the POC. If an upgrade happens, we'll run back-to-back regression on identical inputs and compute delta; quick rollback or mixing rules can be configured in routing.
[06:48] Rachel: Cost expectations?
[06:50] Maya: We'll provide an estimate in the SOW; high-level: hosted baseline may cost X for 2k-5k regression run, Dedicated has monthly commit but lower unit cost at scale. We'll include quantized model options for cost/latency tradeoffs.
[07:05] Aisha: Any recommended prompt engineering to reduce hallucinations?
[07:09] Liam: Structured prompts, explicit output schema, step-by-step chain-of-thought suppression, and instructing model to say "Unknown" instead of guessing. Also use retrieval augmentation for factual grounding if available. We'll include prompt templates in the shared doc.
[07:26] Maya: On evaluation artifacts we'll share: 1) golden prompt spreadsheet, 2) regression harness (python + docker), 3) scoring notebook and metrics dashboard, 4) benchmark scripts for latency/cost. Links will be in the follow-up email.
[07:41] Carlos: For hallucination checks do you support human-in-the-loop review tooling?
[07:45] Liam: Yes — Redwood Console supports review queues and annotation export; we can surface flagged outputs and route to your SMEs for labeling.
[07:55] Rachel: Good. Let's make acceptance criteria explicit in the SOW: weighted score >= 0.85, hallucination_rate < 2%, p95 latency < 450ms for short prompts, and format compliance > 98% for required fields.
[08:12] Maya: We'll draft that and include it. Anything else?
[08:16] Samir: Please include KMS integration details and SOC2 timeline.
[08:19] Maya: Will do.
[08:22] Aisha: One more thing — for the golden set please include at least 10 edge cases where the note is sparse or has ambiguous abbreviations.
[08:29] Liam: Noted. We'll seed 30 that cover edge cases.
[08:33] Jenna: We'll also provide expected schemas and a mapping doc.
[08:36] Maya: Perfect. Recap of next steps and owners, then we'll close.
[08:42] Maya: (recap) Maya to share SOW by Friday. Liam to seed eval harness. ZenHealth to share data and golden examples. Security session next week.
[09:00] Rachel: Thanks everyone.
[09:03] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with links.
